children.value: > Fact From Story: Inconsistency breeds uncertainty.

> > Fact From Story: The U.K. government isn’t willing to be consistent when it comes to climate crisis response policy, which, aside from capital and the support of nascent tech markets, is one of the most critical things anyone in our sector can hope for.
> > > Fact From Story: Sunak has pushed back the British net-zero transition timeline by at least five years.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Delaying a transition is inconsistent.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Climate tech businesses need consistency in policy to thrive.
> Fact From Story: For entrepreneurs, innovators and businesses to thrive and unlock the economic potential that comes from creating new industries, we need a consistent approach from the government.

> > Fact From Story: We wouldn’t have affordable solar panels, microchips, mobile phones or the internet without government funding, government subsidies, government encouragement and government infrastructure.

> > > > Fact From Story: In January of this year, Chancellor Jeremy Hunt unveiled a long-term vision to grow the economy, saying, “I want the world’s tech entrepreneurs, life science innovators and clean energy companies to come to the U.K. because it offers the best possible place to make their vision happen.”
> > > > Fact From Story: All major technological innovation ultimately comes from government support at the very beginning.
> > > > Commonsense Knowledge: Government funding, subsidies, encouragement, and infrastructure are forms of government support.
> > Fact From Story: All major technological innovation ultimately comes from government support at the very beginning.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Government support requires consistent policy.
